# `lost-error-context`

<!-- rule-docs:header (generated by `zig build rule-docs`) -->
Tier: style · Profile: strict · Default: off · Fixes: none · Options: none

Reports a catch that maps every failure to one replacement error without using
the captured original error.
<!-- /rule-docs:header -->

## Why it matters

Collapsing distinct failures removes evidence needed for diagnosis and can make
callers handle the wrong abstraction.

## When it fires

Enable it at error-boundary code where preserving identity, logging context, or
deliberate translation is expected. An operation that can fail in only one way
loses nothing when that error keeps its name (`allocator.alloc(...) catch
return error.OutOfMemory`), when checked arithmetic's `error.Overflow`
becomes a domain limit (`std.math.add(...) catch return error.TooLarge`), or
when it becomes the `error.WriteFailed` a `*std.Io.Writer` implementation must
report; an allocating writer's `WriteFailed` reported as `OutOfMemory` is the
same failure. These are not reported. The single error is known for
`std.math` arithmetic (`Overflow`), allocator methods and `allocPrint`
(`OutOfMemory`), `bufPrint` (`NoSpaceLeft`), `*std.Io.Writer` methods
(`WriteFailed`) on a receiver declared as a `Writer` or taken from an
`Allocating` writer's `writer` or a file writer's `interface`, and functions
the file declares with a one-error set (`Allocator.Error`, `Writer.Error`,
`error{Name}` or an alias of one). Functions declared in other files are not
resolved, so a call such as `tree.renderError(err, w)` stays reported.

<!-- rule-docs:footer (generated by `zig build rule-docs`) -->
## Example

```zig
fn load() !void {
    return error.Failed;
}

fn open() !void {
    load() catch return error.LoadFailed;
}
```

Reference: <https://ziglang.org/documentation/master/#Errors>
